author: pyup-bot
body:
### Update [astropy](https://pypi.org/project/astropy) from **5.1.1** to **7.0.1**.


<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.0.1
   ```
   ==========================

API Changes
-----------

astropy.table
^^^^^^^^^^^^^

- The use of the keyword ``use_local_files`` for the js viewer in
  ``astropy.table.Table.show_in_browser`` is now deprecated. Starting in Astropy
  7.1 this keyword will be ignored and use of it will issue a warning. The
  default behavior will be to use the remote versions of jQuery and DataTables
  from a CDN. [17480]

Bug Fixes
---------

astropy.config
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

- With ``astropy`` v7.0.0 the cache directory cannot be customized with the
  ``XDG_CACHE_HOME`` environment variable.
  Instead, ``XDG_CONFIG_HOME`` erroneously controls both configuration and cache
  directories.
  The correct pre-v7.0.0 behaviour has been restored, but it is possible that
  ``astropy`` v7.0.0 has written cache files to surprising locations.
  Concerned users can use the ``get_cache_dir_path()`` function to check where
  the cache files are written.

  The bug in question does not affect systems where the ``XDG_CACHE_HOME`` and
  ``XDG_CONFIG_HOME`` environment variables are unset. [17514]

astropy.coordinates
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

- Fixed a numerical-precision bug with the calculation of the ``theta``
  component when converting from ``CylindricalRepresentation`` to
  ``PhysicsSphericalRepresentation`` for vectors very close to the Z axis (within
  milliarcseconds). [17693]

astropy.io.ascii
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

- Fixed parsing ASCII table with data that starts with a tilda. [17565]

- Find and read ASCII tables even if there is white space before
  ``\begin{tabular}``, ``\tablehead``, and similar markers. [17624]

astropy.io.fits
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

- Fix memory leak in BinTableHDU.copy() [16143]

- Fix overflow error with Numpy 2 and VLA columns using P format. [17328]

- Fix ``ImageHDU.scale`` with float. [17458]

- Fixed ``Table.write(..., format="fits", overwrite=True)`` when filename is
  provided as ``pathlib.Path``. [17552]

astropy.io.votable
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

- Updated XML writer for ``VOTableFile`` element to include or drop
  ``coordinate_systems`` regardless of version. [17356]

astropy.modeling
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

- Fix fitting of compound models when inputs has more than one dimension, and
  specifically fix fitting of compound models with Polynomial2D components
  [17618]

astropy.table
^^^^^^^^^^^^^

- Ensure that representations and differentials, like SkyCoord, can be used in
  table join operations, by making use of the fact that they can now be masked. [17381]

- Fix a crash in ``Table.show_in_browser`` due to an internal type inconsistency. [17513]

- Fix incorrect description of the ``unique`` parameter in ``Table.add_index``'s
  docstring. Add missing Raises section. [17677]

astropy.units
^^^^^^^^^^^^^

- Ensure that ``Unit.to`` allows as ``value`` argument all array types that
  follow the array API standard and define ``__array_namespace__``. Furthermore,
  for backwards compatibility, generally pass through arguments that define a
  ``.dtype``, independent of whether that is a numpy data type. [17469]

- The zebi (Zi, 2^70) and yobi (Yi, 2^80) binary prefixes are now supported. [17692]

astropy.visualization
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

- Fix ``CoordinateHelper.ticklabels``. The getter was incorrectly returning
  the helper's ticks rather than the labels. [17444]

- The following private classes from ``astropy.visualization.lupton_rgb``, that
  were dropped without deprecation in astropy 7.0.0, were re-introduced following
  a report that they were used downstream. The following classes are now
  considered public:

  - ``Mapping``
  - ``AsinhMapping``
  - ``LinearMapping``
  - ``AsinhZScaleMapping`` [17531]

Other Changes and Additions
---------------------------

- Update bundled js library datatables to version 2.1.8, which is current at the time of this PR. [17480]
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.0.0
   ```
   ==========================


New Features
------------

astropy.config
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

- Added ``get_config_dir_path`` (and ``get_cache_dir_path``) which is equivalent
  to ``get_config_dir`` (respectively ``get_cache_dir``) except that it returns a
  ``pathlib.Path`` object instead of ``str``. [17118]

astropy.coordinates
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

- ``BaseCoordinateFrame`` instances such as ``ICRS``, ``SkyOffsetFrame``, etc.,
  can now be stored directly in tables (previously, they were stored as
  ``object`` type columns). Furthermore, storage in tables is now also possible
  for frames that have no data (but which have attributes with the correct shape
  to fit in the table). [16831]

- ``BaseCoordinateFrame`` now has a ``to_table()`` method, which converts the
  frame to a ``QTable``, analogously to the ``SkyCoord.to_table()`` method. [17009]

- ``SkyCoord``, coordinate frames, and representations have all have gained the
  ability to deal with ``Masked`` data. In general, the procedure is similar to
  that of ``Time``, except that different representation components do not share
  the mask, to enable holding, e.g., a catalogue of objects in which only some
  have associated distances. [17016]

astropy.io.ascii
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

- Add support for ``pathlib.Path`` objects in
  ``astropy.io.ascii.core.BaseInputter.get_lines``. [16930]

astropy.io.fits
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

- Expanded ``FITSDiff`` output for ``PrimaryHDU`` and ``ImageHDU`` to include the
  maximum relative and absolute differences in the data. [17097]

astropy.io.misc
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

- The HDF5 writer, ``write_table_hdf5()``, now accepts ``os.PathLike`` objects
  as ``output``. [16955]

astropy.io.votable
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

- Support reading and writing of VOTable version 1.5, including the new
  ``refposition`` attribute of ``COOSYS``. [16856]

astropy.modeling
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

- Added ``Model.has_tied``, ``Model.has_fixed``, and ``Model.has_bounds`` attributes to make
  it easy to check whether models have various kinds of constraints set without having to
  inspect ``Model.tied``, ``Model.fixed``, and ``Model.bounds`` in detail. [16677]

- Added a new ``parallel_fit_dask`` function that can be used to fit models to
  many sections (e.g. spectra, image slices) on an N-dimensional array in
  parallel. [16696]

- Added a ``Lorentz2D`` model. [16800]

- Added ``inplace=False/True`` keyword argument to the ``__call__`` method of most fitters,
  to optionally allow the original model passed to the fitter to be modified with the fitted
  values of the parameters, rather than return a copy. This can improve performance if users
  don't need to keep hold of the initial parameter values. [17033]

astropy.stats
^^^^^^^^^^^^^

- Added a ``SigmaClippedStats`` convenience class for computing sigma-clipped
  statistics. [17221]

astropy.table
^^^^^^^^^^^^^

- Changed a number of dict-like containers in ``io.ascii`` from ``OrderedDict`` to
  ``dict``. The ``dict`` class maintains key order since Python 3.8 so ``OrderedDict`` is
  no longer needed. The changes are largely internal and should not affect users in any
  way. See also the API change log entry for this PR. [16250]

- Add a ``keep_order`` argument to the ``astropy.table.join`` function which specifies to
  maintain the original order of the key table in the joined output. This applies for
  inner, left, and right joins. The default is ``False`` in which case the output is
  ordered by the join keys, consistent with prior behavior. [16361]

astropy.units
^^^^^^^^^^^^^

- Add a ``formatter`` argument to the ``to_string`` method of the ``Quantity``
  class. Enables custom number formatting with a callable formatter or
  format_spec, especially useful for consistent notation. [16087]

- Add the unit foe (or Bethe, equivalent to 1e51 erg), which is often used to
  express the energy emitted by a supernova explosion. [16441]

- Add ``magnetic_flux_field`` equivalency to conver

author: bblommers
body:
The `ruff` formatter is not yet stable, but it makes sense (IMO) to update to the latest version as much as possible, to reduce the amount of changes we'll have to make when `ruff` 1.0 releases.

The latest version of `ruff` supports a ton more of `pylint`'s rules. The ones that are not covered yet, but that we had enabled:
 - arguments-renamed
 - deprecated-module
 - redefined-outer-name
 - signature-differs

I'm sure that thse rules will be part of `ruff` at some point, but in the mean time, I propose we drop `pylint` altogether. Validation of these 4 rules is nice, but it's not worth the time it takes `pylint` to run (again, IMHO).

@bpandola What do you think - any objections to this?

body:
This pull request introduces significant enhancements to the Daebus framework, focusing on enabling concurrent message processing, improving thread safety, and optimizing the handling of shared state. Key changes include the addition of a thread pool for concurrent message processing, thread-local storage for request and response objects, and updates to the proxy classes to support concurrency. These updates aim to improve performance, scalability, and thread safety in multi-service environments.

### Concurrent Message Processing

* Added support for concurrent message processing using a configurable thread pool (`max_workers` parameter, default: 10). This allows multiple incoming messages to be processed simultaneously without blocking each other. (`README.md` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R471-R581) `daebus/modules/daemon.py` [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-563f57a09954295d3eee1a1d785258bd99d20c2eee5f9a8dd9b5386568052f47L16-R17) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-563f57a09954295d3eee1a1d785258bd99d20c2eee5f9a8dd9b5386568052f47R34-R35) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-563f57a09954295d3eee1a1d785258bd99d20c2eee5f9a8dd9b5386568052f47R256-R259) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-563f57a09954295d3eee1a1d785258bd99d20c2eee5f9a8dd9b5386568052f47L282-R290) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-563f57a09954295d3eee1a1d785258bd99d20c2eee5f9a8dd9b5386568052f47L302-R307)

### Thread Safety Enhancements

* Introduced thread-local storage for `request` and `response` objects, ensuring isolated contexts for each thread. Added helper methods to set, get, and clear these thread-local variables. (`daebus/modules/context.py` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-21b3d56f0691f0811dcf87793a4a95936b78182f013ee979c2c9a33c86c48eb0L11-R11) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-21b3d56f0691f0811dcf87793a4a95936b78182f013ee979c2c9a33c86c48eb0R66-R171)
* Updated `RequestProxy` and `ResponseProxy` classes to support thread-local objects, enabling concurrent access while maintaining backward compatibility. (`daebus/modules/context.py` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-21b3d56f0691f0811dcf87793a4a95936b78182f013ee979c2c9a33c86c48eb0L131-R230) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-21b3d56f0691f0811dcf87793a4a95936b78182f013ee979c2c9a33c86c48eb0L146-R255) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-21b3d56f0691f0811dcf87793a4a95936b78182f013ee979c2c9a33c86c48eb0L188-R319) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-21b3d56f0691f0811dcf87793a4a95936b78182f013ee979c2c9a33c86c48eb0L202-R349)

### Proxy Class Improvements

* Enhanced `_Proxy` class to handle thread-local objects and provide better error handling for missing daemon attributes. (`daebus/modules/context.py` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-21b3d56f0691f0811dcf87793a4a95936b78182f013ee979c2c9a33c86c48eb0R66-R171) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-21b3d56f0691f0811dcf87793a4a95936b78182f013ee979c2c9a33c86c48eb0L243-R420)
* Added no-op methods for common Pub/Sub response methods (`success`, `error`, `progress`) to improve testability and error handling in the absence of a daemon. (`daebus/modules/context.py` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-21b3d56f0691f0811dcf87793a4a95936b78182f013ee979c2c9a33c86c48eb0L146-R255) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-21b3d56f0691f0811dcf87793a4a95936b78182f013ee979c2c9a33c86c48eb0L202-R349) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-21b3d56f0691f0811dcf87793a4a95936b78182f013ee979c2c9a33c86c48eb0L221-R401)

### Documentation Updates

* Updated the `README.md` file to document the new concurrent processing features, thread safety mechanisms, and performance considerations. Provided examples for configuring the thread pool and implementing thread-safe shared state. (`README.md` [README.mdR471-R581](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R471-R581))

These changes collectively enhance the framework's ability to handle high-throughput, concurrent workloads while maintaining thread safety and resource efficiency.

author: flash1293
body:
The ESQL histogram breakdown-by functionality uses a simple `STATS by {field name}`. This works OK, but it does not take into account that some docs do not have a value for a field.

This can be very confusing, especially for the case where a default breakdown field is selected, like in the case of the logs profile, which picks `log.level` by default - in this case, the histogram doesn't show all the data it matches but just a subset. It's common for datasets to only have log.level set on a subset of logs.

This PR fixes this problem by using a `COALESCE` function to show docs without a value for the breakdown field as `<missing>`.

To quote @nik9000

> COALESCE is pretty much free if the block doesn't have any null values in it.

This PR introduces a new standalone Share module (`share.html` + `share.js`) to enable **private chart sharing between users**. The module is fully functional and supports:

- Creating new shares (chart + recipient)
- Tracking sent and received shares
- Withdrawing previously shared charts
- Jumping to shared charts in `visualize.html?id=xxx`
- Highlighting shared charts upon load
- Collapsible sent/received sections for better UX
- Responsive design & smooth visual transitions

###  Technical Details

- Shares are saved via localStorage (can later be integrated into backend)
- Uses `chartId` as visual link parameter for jump
- Sent shares are shown with timestamp + withdrawal button
- UI follows the same layout as the dashboard, styled with additions to `style.css`
- CSS additions are grouped under `/* Share Page Styles */` section for clarity

###  Compatibility

- This module does **not conflict with existing Share buttons in `visualize.html`**
- Runs as an independent page at `share.html`
- Future integration possible if team prefers a unified share flow

body:
This pull request introduces several enhancements and fixes to the configuration management and initialization flow of the application. Key changes include the addition of a method to modify configurations dynamically, improvements to configuration serialization/deserialization, and better error handling.

### Enhancements to Configuration Management:
* Added a new `ModifyConfig` method in `controllers/controller.cs` to allow users to update the configuration dynamically during runtime. This includes updating the source, destination, and language settings, and reloading projects with the new configuration.
* Updated `InitializeForm` in `view/view.cs` to use exact property names (`Source`, `Destination`, `Language`) for consistency with the new configuration model.

### Improvements to Configuration Serialization:
* Changed the `JsonSerializerOptions` in `models/modelConfig.cs` to use exact property names instead of camel case, ensuring consistency between serialized and deserialized property names.
* Updated the `Load` and `Save` methods in `models/modelConfig.cs` to handle configuration properties dynamically and added error logging for better debugging. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-44cf44e67ed084af59f3f97abba2f21043d3552331bbba8815b843cb1e62fcdbL48-R63) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-44cf44e67ed084af59f3f97abba2f21043d3552331bbba8815b843cb1e62fcdbL81-R105)

### Minor Fixes and Adjustments:
* Fixed a typo in the `Initialization` method of `controllers/controller.cs` (`Toogle AutoSave` corrected to `Toggle AutoSave`).
* Refactored the `Controller` class constructor to initialize all fields explicitly, improving readability and maintainability.

author: hertzdevil
body:
Resolves #14376.

Setting `LLVM_VERSION` as an environment variable or a command-line argument to `make` will now inhibit LLVM version detection via `LLVM_CONFIG`. This is mainly to support cross-compilation from Linux to Windows MSVC, i.e. `make crystal target=x86_64-windows-msvc LLVM_VERSION=19.1.7` should now just work on WSL. It is also advisable to set the `LLVM_TARGETS` and `LLVM_LDFLAGS` environment variables, as implemented in #15091.

Using LLVM 17 or below will still fail if `LLVM_CONFIG` is not set, since the Makefiles have never supported cross-compiling `llvm_ext.o`, and that object file needs `llvm-config --cxxflags`.

A side benefit is that Crystal can now somewhat target future LLVM versions by simply doing something like `make LLVM_VERSION=21.0.0`, since it is only `find-llvm-config.sh` that imposes the version check.

body: # PR 제목 차ㅏㅏㅏㅏㅏㅏㅏㅏㅏㅏㅏㅏㅏㅁ 길다ㅏㅏㅏㅏㅏㅏㅏㅏㅏㅏㅏㅏㅏㅏ ## 들어가기 전에 백엔드에서 이미지 저장을 어떻게 구현할까요? 1. 서버 컴퓨터에 걍 파일 저장 후 디비에 저장경로 문자열만 저장 -> 직관적이고 쉽지만 용량, 관리(보안, 백업 직접 해야..) 등 몇 단점이 있음 2. 바이너리 데이터인 이미지를 base64로 String으로 변환해 DB에 저장? -> 원본 이미지보다도 용량이 훨씬 커지고 인/디코딩 작업 필수. 몰입캠프때 해봤는데 심지어 몽고디비에선 이렇게 하면 디비 화면이 렉걸려 아예 뻗어버림. trash idea. 3. 국룰방식인 클라우드 저장소를 이용합시다(aws s3, firebase storage ..) 우리 프로젝트에선 AWS S3 bucket을 쓰며 업로드 방식은 최근 트렌드인 **PresignedUrl 방식**을 사용합니다. ## 이미지 저장 플로우 게시글 생성의 상황으로 설명합니다. 1. 클라이언트가 게시글 입력값과 이미지를 넣고 게시글 생성 버튼 클릭 2. 프론트는 게시글 생성버튼을 누를 때 내부적으로 총 3개의 api를 호출해야함. (중간에 오류시 예외 리턴) [⭐️ 하단 api 호출 전 게시글 생성 api request 입력값 프론트에서 validation을 먼저 해야합니다.] a. `/api/aws/presigned-url` : 이미지를 클라우드에 저장할 수 있는 api 경로, 즉 **presignedUrl을 발급받습니다.** 백엔드에서 해당 이미지를 s3 bucket에 저장 요청할 경로인 **presignedUrl**과 저장된 이미지에 접근 가능한 주소인 **publicUrl**을 리턴받습니다. b. a로부터 얻은 presignedUrl에 다음처럼 PUT 요청을 보냅니다. 헤더도 동일하게 해야합니다. PR의 s3-test.html 중 이미지 업로드 코드의 일부입니다 c. `/api/posts` : 이미지가 무사히 업로드 됐다면 게시글 생성 요청값에서 imageUrl 리스트에 publicUrl들을 담고 게시글 생성 api를 호출합니다. 그럼 자연스래 생각이 드는게 "**c에서 에러터지면? 클라우드엔 이미지가 업로드 돼버렸는데?**"일 것입니다. - 그래서 상술했듯이 a 호출 전 validation이 필요합니다. 이러면 b -> c 플로우는 정상적으로 작동됩니다. ## 마무리 - 구현 사항 설명은 여기 남기기엔 너무 길어져 파일 코멘트에 직접 남겼습니다. - ~~localhost:8080/s3-test.html로 이미지 업로드 및 조회기능 테스트 매~우 간단하게 해볼 수 있습니다. 심심하면 ㄱㄱ~~ - 2차 PR 하면서 presignedUrl에 jwt 인증 요구돼서 그냥 postman으로 테스트해야합니다 ㅜ +) 5/13 jwt token을 uuid 대신 userId, nickname을 쓰는 것으로 변경했고 코멘트를 반영해서 재커밋했습니다 closes #41

author: joewalabel
body:
Added the option to show/hide coordinates by pressing a hotkey. Default: Insert

You can assign more than one key.
You must use Unity KeyCode names: https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/KeyCode.html
The hotkey is configurable in the config file and multiple keys must be separated by '+'.
Example:
LeftShift + RightControl + Alpha0

Crash prevention:

    Checks for invalid keys and falls back to the default (Insert)

    Adds a small delay between key presses to prevent the toggle from running multiple times

author: hardcode84
body:
I'm planning to retire `dynamic_symbols_map` eventually and extract symbol values directly from the input tensor dimensions. One exception is `extend_attention` which have `MAX_EXTEND_SEQ_LEN` symbol which does not correspond to any input tensor dimension.

As we now support scalar codegen, instead of using `dynamic_symbols_map` we now can just pass `MAX_EXTEND_SEQ_LEN` directly as kernel argument.

Extend attention is using `MAX_EXTEND_SEQ_LEN` for grid dimension calculation so normal scalar + `set_symbol` won't work. Instead, introduce `SymbolBind` annotation, which works exactly like scalar arg, but also immediately binds value to the corresponding symbol.

Most of the codegen changes are to propagate scalar args to the dispatch dims and to generally support scalar args in iree runtime path.

author: keysmashes
body:
As I mentioned in [the Discourse thread about the recent breaking change to PAM configuration](https://discourse.nixos.org/t/re-recent-breaking-changes-lockscreen-pam/63719/28?u=keysmashes), I think it would be a good idea to include a link to [the breaking changes announcement thread on Discourse](https://discourse.nixos.org/t/17574) in the PR template checklist.

That thread seems extremely valuable to me, since (unlike the release notes here on GitHub) you can subscribe to it and be notified about breaking changes automatically. However, it's not particularly widely-used: it saw 4 posts so far this year (which we are 35% of the way through), 32 posts last year, and 24 posts in 2023, which is pretty clearly far behind the number of breaking changes included in the release notes (at time of writing, 114 bulletpoints under "Backward Incompatibilities" in the [Nixpkgs 25.05 release notes](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/c5427604c76fa5a4bf33f113fe54e4a3f64e1e8d/doc/release-notes/rl-2505.section.md), and 63 in the [NixOS 25.05 release notes](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/c5427604c76fa5a4bf33f113fe54e4a3f64e1e8d/nixos/doc/manual/release-notes/rl-2505.section.md)). This limits its utility.

Perhaps the thread will be uselessly noisy if every breaking change is posted there. On the other hand, perhaps it will become more useful with a more comprehensive view of breaking changes. Perhaps it will reveal that some things marked as breaking changes are in fact not: for example, "GIMP 3.0 available as `gimp3`" doesn't strike me as breaking. Maybe we will decide that some things, like "`xdragon` package has been renamed to `dragon-drop`", may not need posting (since `warnOnInstantiate` or `throw` in `pkgs/top-level/aliases.nix` will notify the affected users directly). It's quite hard to suggest strict guidelines up-front; I think it will be quite useful to just try nudging people towards posting there and watching what happens. We can always remove the link if it makes things worse.

author: gaalferov
body:
## Motivation
The integration name `mailtrap+api` caused confusion and potential conflicts with the official Symfony MailtrapMailer package. To avoid ambiguity and ensure better compatibility and clarity, we renamed our integration to `mailtrap+sdk`, which more accurately reflects the method of integration.


## Changes

- [BC BREAK] Change Symfony&Laravel integration naming from `mailtrap+api` to `mailtrap+sdk`. The reason is conflist with official Symfony [MailtrapMailer Package](https://symfony.com/packages/MailtrapMailer))
- Rollback Psalm library because now they support PHP 8.4 (static analyzer)
- Update README and examples

## How to test

```
composer test
```

author: midnightcoder-m
body:
### Pull Request Description
This pull request aims to implement a more robust mechanism to maintain the "lock on position" mode for users, particularly those driving and requiring the ability to zoom, pan, or rotate the map while preserving tracking functionality.

#### **✨ Approach**
- Introduced a 5-second auto-relock mechanism after map panning, ensuring that the map automatically re-centers on the user's position unless explicitly unlocked.
- Added a visual progress bar within the toaster message to indicate the relock timer. This provides users with feedback about the relock countdown.
- Included an "Unlock" button within the toaster message for users to permanently disable auto-relocking if needed.

#### **UI Changes**
- Updated the `Toast.qml` component:
  - Added a new `animationEnabled` property to support animations like the relock countdown.
  - Implemented a progress bar as part of the toast's background to visually display the auto-relock timer.
  - Modified the toast's `show` function to handle additional parameters for animation and stop-action behavior.
- Enhanced `qgismobileapp.qml`:
  - Integrated logic to handle map gestures (panning, zooming, and rotation) that reset the auto-relock timer.
  - Added `autoReFollowLocation` property and related functions (`cancelAutoFollowLocation` and `followLocation`) to manage the relock mechanism.
  - Updated the `displayToast` function to include parameters for the progress bar and unlock functionality.

#### **WIP** 

Zoom gestures and rotation events on Android.

author: mike-popovych
body:
⚠️ Breaking Change: Husky 9.x Hook Initialization
In Husky version 9.x, the way hooks are initialized has changed, leading to a breaking change for projects upgrading from version 8.x.

💥 What Changed:
Previous versions (8.x and below) used a script _husky.sh for hook initialization:


```bash
#!/usr/bin/env sh
. "$(dirname -- "$0")/_/husky.sh"
npm run pre-commit
```
In version 9.x, this initialization script has been removed.

Hooks are now executed directly without using _husky.sh.

✅ New Format:
Simply use:

```bash
npm run pre-commit
```
📝 Why This is a Breaking Change:
If you upgrade without updating your hooks, they will break because _husky.sh no longer exists.

You need to remove the old initialization lines from all your Husky hooks to ensure compatibility.

:information_source: Keep your dependencies up-to-date. This makes it easier to fix existing vulnerabilities and to more quickly identify and fix newly disclosed vulnerabilities when they affect your project.

Release notes
Package name: react-redux
  • 9.2.0 - 2024-12-10

    This feature release updates the React peer dependency to work with React 19, and improves treeshakeability of our build artifacts.

    Changelog

    React 19 Compat

    React 19 was just released! We've updated our peer dep to accept React 19, and updated our runtime and type tests to check against both React 18 and 19.

    Also see Redux Toolkit v2.5.0 for the same peer dep update.

    Treeshaking

    We've done some nitty-gritty optimization work to ensure bundlers correctly treeshake unused parts of the bundle.

    What's Changed

    • Improve treeshakeability of build artifacts by @ aryaemami59 in #2176
    • Migrate to React by @ aryaemami59 in #2172
    • Migrate to React 19 (take 2) by @ markerikson in #2216
    • Clean up devdeps by @ markerikson in #2217

    Full Changelog: v9.1.2...v9.2.0

  • 9.1.2 - 2024-05-02

    This bugfix release removes the no-longer-necessary peer dependency on react-native, and tweaks a few TS types for compat with the upcoming React 19 release.

    Changes

    React Native Peer Dependency Removed

    We've always had an awkward peer dependency on both ReactDOM and React Native, because of the need to import the unstable_batchedUpdates API directly from each reconciler. That's part of what led to the sequence of 9.x patch releases to deal with RN compat.

    As of 9.0.3, we dropped the batching imports completely, since React 18 now batches by default. That means we didn't even have any remaining imports from react-native.

    Meanwhile, React 18.3 just came out, but so did React Native 0.74. RN 0.74 still requires React 18.2.

    This caused NPM users to have installation failures when trying to use React-Redux:

    • React-Redux has a peer dep on RN
    • RN has a peer dep on React 18.2
    • But the latest React, 18.3 would get installed in the app
    • NPM errors with a peer dep mismatch

    We no longer need to list RN as a peer dep, and dropping that also fixes the NPM installation issues as well.

    What's Changed

    • Fix useRef usages to be called with an explicit argument of undefined. by @ aryaemami59 in #2164
    • Replace usage of deprecated JSX global namespace with React.JSX by @ aryaemami59 in #2163
    • Drop now-unneeded RN peer dep by @ markerikson in

Release notes
Package name: redux
  • 5.0.1 - 2023-12-23

    This patch release adjusts the isPlainObject util to allow objects created via Object.create(null), and fixes a type issue which accidentally made the store state type non-nullable.

    What's Changed

    • fix(isPlainObject): support check Object.create(null) by @ zhe-he in #4633
    • fix(types/store): Unexpectedly narrowed return type of function Store['getState'] by @ exuanbo in #4638

    Full Changelog: v5.0.0...v5.0.1

  • 5.0.0 - 2023-12-04

    This major release:

    • Converts the codebase to TypeScript
    • Updates the packaging for better ESM/CJS compatibility and modernizes the build output
    • Requires that action.type must be a string
    • Continues to mark createStore as deprecated
    • Deprecates the AnyAction type in favor of an UnknownAction type that is used everywhere
    • Removes the PreloadedState type in favor of a new generic argument for the Reducer type.

    This release has breaking changes.

    This release is part of a wave of major versions of all the Redux packages: Redux Toolkit 2.0, Redux core 5.0, React-Redux 9.0, Reselect 5.0, and Redux Thunk 3.0.

    For full details on all of the breaking changes and other significant changes to all of those packages, see the "Migrating to RTK 2.0 and Redux 5.0" migration guide in the Redux docs.

    Note

    The Redux core, Reselect, and Redux Thunk packages are included as part of Redux Toolkit, and RTK users do not need to manually upgrade them - you'll get them as part of the upgrade to RTK 2.0. (If you're not using Redux Toolkit yet, please start migrating your existing legacy Redux code to use Redux Toolkit today!)

    # RTK
npm install @ reduxjs/toolkit
yarn add @ reduxjs/toolkit

# Standalone
npm install redux
yarn add redux

    Changelog

    ESM/CJS Package Compatibility

Snyk has created this PR to upgrade redux-thunk from 2.3.0 to 3.1.0.

:information_source: Keep your dependencies up-to-date. This makes it easier to fix existing vulnerabilities and to more quickly identify and fix newly disclosed vulnerabilities when they affect your project.
⚠️ **Warning:** This PR contains major version upgrade(s), and may be a breaking change. - The recommended version is **12 versions** ahead of your current version. - The recommended version was released **a year ago**.
Release notes
Package name: redux-thunk
  • 3.1.0 - 2023-12-04

    This major release:

    • Updates the packaging for better ESM/CJS compatibility
    • Changes the package to use named exports instead of a default export

    This release has breaking changes. (Note: this actually points to v3.1.0, which includes a hotfix that was meant for 3.0.0.)

    This release is part of a wave of major versions of all the Redux packages: Redux Toolkit 2.0, Redux core 5.0, React-Redux 9.0, Reselect 5.0, and Redux Thunk 3.0.

    For full details on all of the breaking changes and other significant changes to all of those packages, see the "Migrating to RTK 2.0 and Redux 5.0" migration guide in the Redux docs.

    Note

    The Redux core, Reselect, and Redux Thunk packages are included as part of Redux Toolkit, and RTK users do not need to manually upgrade them - you'll get them as part of the upgrade to RTK 2.0. (If you're not using Redux Toolkit yet, please start migrating your existing legacy Redux code to use Redux Toolkit today!)

    # RTK
npm install @ reduxjs/toolkit
yarn add @ reduxjs/toolkit

# Standalone
npm install redux-thunk
yarn add redux-thunk

    Changelog

    Named Exports Instead of Default Exports

    The redux-thunk package previously used a single default export that was the thunk middleware, with an attached field named withExtraArgument that allowed customization.

    The default export has been removed. There are now two named exports: thunk (the basic middleware) and withExtraArgument.

    If you are using Redux Toolkit, this should have no effect, as RTK already handles this inside of configureStore.

    ESM/CJS Package Compatibility

    The biggest theme of the Redux v5 and RTK 2.0 releases is trying to get "true" ESM package publishing compatibility in place, while still supporting CJS in the published package.

    The primary build artifact is now an ESM file, dist/redux-thunk.mjs. Most build tools should pick this up. There's also a CJS artifact, and a second copy of the ESM file named redux-thunk.legacy-esm.js to support Webpack 4 (which does not recognize the exports field in package.json).

    Build Tooling

    We're now building the package using https://github.com/egoist/tsup. We also now include sourcemaps for the ESM and CJS artifacts.

    The repo has been updated to use Yarn 3 for dependencies and Vitest for running tests.

    Dropping UMD Builds

    Redux has always shipped with UMD build artifacts. These are primarily meant for direct import as script tags, such as in a CodePen or a no-bundler build environment.

    For now, we're dropping those build artifacts from the published package, on the grounds that the use cases seem pretty rare today.

    Since the code is so simple, the ESM artifact can be used directly in the browser via Unpkg.

    If you have strong use cases for us continuing to include UMD build artifacts, please let us know!

    extend-redux Typedefs Removed

    Redux Thunk 2.x included a redux-thunk/extend-redux TS-only entry point, which extended the types of dispatch and bindActionCreators to globally give them knowledge of the thunk types. We feel that global overrides from a library are an anti-pattern, and we've removed this entry point. (Note: this ended up being released in 3.1.0, as it was missed in the original 3.0.0 release.)

    Please follow our TS setup guidelines to infer the correct type of dispatch for your store.

    What's Changed

    • Migrate thunk package to ESM by @ markerikson in #340
    • Switch package manager to Yarn 3 and update CI jobs by @ markerikson in #341
    • Run RTK publish CI examples on built artifact by @ markerikson in #342
    • Rewrite build/test setup and hopefully fix ESM comp

author: siliconvalleyvigo
body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/SiliconValleyVigo/wairbot.es/security/code-scanning/9](https://github.com/SiliconValleyVigo/wairbot.es/security/code-scanning/9)

To fix the issue, we need to sanitize or encode the value of `window.location.href` before using it in the `htmlLogin` string. A safe approach is to use a library like `DOMPurify` to sanitize the URL or encode it using `encodeURIComponent` or similar methods. This ensures that any potentially malicious content in the URL is neutralized before being inserted into the DOM.

The best fix for this issue is to sanitize `thisUrl` before it is used in the `htmlLogin` string. We will use `encodeURIComponent` to encode the URL, which is sufficient for this context since the URL is being used as part of an `src` attribute.

author: rasulkireev
body:
This commit introduces two main enhancements to the blog functionality:

1.  **Published Post Filtering:** The `BlogPostView` (detail view) now filters blog posts to only display those marked with `BlogPostStatus.PUBLISHED`. This prevents users from accessing draft or otherwise unpublished posts directly.

2.  **Enhanced Meta Image Handling:** The `blog_post.html` template has been updated to provide a fallback mechanism for images used in OpenGraph, Twitter card, and JSON-LD metadata. The image selection order is now:
    - `blog_post.image`
    - `blog_post.icon` (if `image` is not present)
    - Default static logo (if neither `image` nor `icon` is present) This ensures that social sharing previews and search engine results always have an associated image.

Additionally, the display of `post.icon` has been removed from the main blog listing page (`blog_posts.html`). This change aims to improve the visual consistency or simplify the layout of the blog index.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **New Features**
	- Blog post detail pages now only display published posts.
- **Improvements**
	- Blog post detail pages dynamically select the most appropriate image for sharing and structured data, using the main image, icon, or a default logo as available.
- **Style**
	- Blog post listing pages no longer display post icons, resulting in a cleaner appearance.

author: piyushpatle26
body:
This pull request addresses [#300](https://github.com/elogind/elogind/issues/300).
The configuration file 10-elogind.conf includes a misleading comment:
```
# See sleep.conf(5) for details.
```
This reference is incorrect, as the file is related to ```elogind``` configuration, not ```sleep.conf```.

```
-# See sleep.conf(5) for details.
+# See logind.conf(5) for details.
```

This corrects the documentation to point users and developers to the appropriate manual page (logind.conf(5)), improving clarity and usability.

author: ezzargg
body:
This PR introduces the BackupManager class, which handles the creation, deletion, updating, and execution of backup jobs. It incorporates functionality for managing job states, including saving and loading states to/from a JSON file. Backup jobs can be executed, and their states are tracked in real-time during execution. The code also includes the Backup model, which defines the structure for backup job properties.

Key Changes:

BackupManager Class:

Manages a list of backup jobs (_jobs) and their states (_jobStates).

Adds functionality to:

Add new jobs (AddJob).

Remove existing jobs (RemoveJob).

Update job details (UpdateJob).

Execute jobs by indices (ExecuteJobsByIndices).

Run backups for individual jobs with real-time state updates during execution (RunBackup).

Save and load backup states from a JSON file (SaveStates and LoadOrInitializeStates).

Display log entries and errors during backup execution (ShowLogs).

Backup Model:

A new model Backup has been added to store properties like:

Job name

Source and target paths

Backup type (Full or Differential)

File length

Improvements and Features:

State Tracking:

The state of each backup job (including active files, file sizes, and current source/target) is tracked and updated in real-time during backup execution.

Logging:

Logs are generated for key actions (job creation, deletion, update, execution start, completion, and errors).

Errors are logged but don’t interrupt backup of subsequent files.

Backup Execution:

File copying logic is wrapped in try-catch blocks, with appropriate logging for both success and failure.

Active backup states are displayed in the console during job execution.

author: mattsturgeon
body:
> [!NOTE]
> This PR is comprised of intentionally separate commits, please don't squash :slightly_smiling_face:

The global `stylix.enable` option is not relevant to the per-target `enable` option's default. Instead it should be checked in addition to the per-target `enable` option so that is is effective even when a target is explicitly enabled.

Since the target module has to check the global enable separately from the per-target enable, including it in the per-target option's value has no effect.

I spotted this while working on #1244. It felt odd that enable options had a seemingly redundant default: `stylix.enable && stylix.autoEnable`.

See also: https://github.com/danth/stylix/issues/543
Closes: https://github.com/danth/stylix/pull/419

### Example

To give a concrete example of where this default doesn't make sense:

```nix
{
  stylix.enable = false;
  stylix.autoEnable = true;
  stylix.targets.foo.enable = true;
}
```

Here, the `stylix.enable` option is set to `false`, so no targets should be enabled, regardless of their per-target `enable` option's value.

However if the `foo` target assumes it only needs to read its own `enable` option, in this example it would define its config even though Stylix is disabled globally.

- Changed the `mkEnableTarget` default.
- Added a note to the docs, clarifying that a target module must always check `stylix.enable` in addition to its own `enable` option.
- Searched treewide for problematic modules; fixed the three issues I found.

author: ursisterbtw
body:
This pull request introduces significant enhancements to the configuration management, pipeline processing, and markdown chunking functionalities in the `RAGnificent` project. Key changes include support for multiple configuration file formats, improved handling of enums in the pipeline, and enriched metadata for markdown chunking. These updates aim to make the system more flexible, robust, and user-friendly.

### Configuration Enhancements:
* Added support for loading configurations from YAML, JSON, and `.env` files. Introduced methods to save configurations to files and load configurations from directories with layered overrides. (`RAGnificent/core/config.py`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-27f12a154f2c671888522b671bd1066e5379b0e633cdde6cd94fdd184b91cc4fR6-R15) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-27f12a154f2c671888522b671bd1066e5379b0e633cdde6cd94fdd184b91cc4fR461-R512) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-27f12a154f2c671888522b671bd1066e5379b0e633cdde6cd94fdd184b91cc4fL430-R633)
* Enhanced the `AppConfig` class to accept an optional dictionary override and update configurations dynamically using the new `update_from_dict` method. (`RAGnificent/core/config.py`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-27f12a154f2c671888522b671bd1066e5379b0e633cdde6cd94fdd184b91cc4fL361-R370) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-27f12a154f2c671888522b671bd1066e5379b0e633cdde6cd94fdd184b91cc4fR382-R425)

### Pipeline Improvements:
* Improved handling of enums such as `EmbeddingModelType` and `OutputFormat` by converting strings to enums where necessary. This ensures type safety and consistency. (`RAGnificent/rag/pipeline.py`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-133a3fcbb92d305d3f4298c610c8b9b3ef0154385fcd599f9e84998a99b7629eL14-R16) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-133a3fcbb92d305d3f4298c610c8b9b3ef0154385fcd599f9e84998a99b7629eR91-R102) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-133a3fcbb92d305d3f4298c610c8b9b3ef0154385fcd599f9e84998a99b7629eR133-R141)
* Enhanced robustness in embedding and storing chunks by ensuring proper type checks and handling edge cases, such as empty lists or invalid inputs. (`RAGnificent/rag/pipeline.py`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-133a3fcbb92d305d3f4298c610c8b9b3ef0154385fcd599f9e84998a99b7629eL532-R561) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-133a3fcbb92d305d3f4298c610c8b9b3ef0154385fcd599f9e84998a99b7629eR586-R588) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-133a3fcbb92d305d3f4298c610c8b9b3ef0154385fcd599f9e84998a99b7629eL588-R630)
* Improved sitemap parsing by extracting URL strings and applying limits after parsing. (`RAGnificent/rag/pipeline.py`)

### Markdown Chunking Enhancements:
* Added support for richer metadata in markdown chunks, including `parent_headers`, `path_elements`, `nested_level`, and `is_continuation`. This provides better context and structure for downstream processing. (`RAGnificent/utils/chunk_utils.py`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c4601ae2dc545c36f573f0111ba3bad84083fe9b88d98e5462869be4c513b57aR68-R69) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c4601ae2dc545c36f573f0111ba3bad84083fe9b88d98e5462869be4c513b57aR83-R88) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-c4601ae2dc545c36f573f0111ba3bad84083fe9b88d98e5462869be4c513b57aR136-R143)
* Improved context handling in chunk creation by including parent headers and ensuring proper formatting of chunk content. (`RAGnificent/utils/chunk_utils.py`)

These changes collectively enhance the flexibility, maintainability, and usability of the `RAGnificent` system.

## Summary by Sourcery

Enhance configuration management with multi-format file support, layered overrides, and dynamic updates; improve pipeline enum handling and chunk processing robustness; and enrich markdown chunking with detailed metadata and better nested header support.

New Features:
- Add support for loading and saving configuration in YAML, JSON, and .env formats.
- Enable loading and merging multiple configuration files from a directory with layered overrides.
- Support dynamic configuration updates via dictionary overrides.
- Enrich markdown chunk metadata with parent headers, path elements, nested level, and continuation flags.

Enhancements:
- Improve enum handling in pipeline by converting strings to enums for type safety.
- Increase robustness in embedding and storing chunks by handling edge cases and type checks.
- Enhance markdown chunking to better preserve context and structure for nested headers.

Documentation:
- Add example configuration files and documentation for configuration management.

Tests:
- Add comprehensive unit tests for configuration file support and nested header chunking.

Chores:
- Remove legacy sitemap implementation and update project roadmap.

author: squell
body:
With these fixes we are still generating them for every release, but now they are in the repo which can help for packaging.

I don't like putting them in separate folders (TROFF isn't a "compiled" thing, so calling them precompiled as is done in Pendulum is a bit of a misnomer); it's not unconceivable someone might want to read the manpages using `man` so then it makes sense to have them in the same place.

We could considered adding a CI step that checks for coherence, but decided against that: it wasted time writing that CI step, wastes developer time by making the CI yet more costly (the whole pandoc things runs in a docker...), and the only problem it solves is the remote possibility that someone mistakenly edits the `.man` file instead of the `.md` file. So let's be  pragmatic.

This PR implements the NIP-50 user search requested in issue #9.

## Changes:
- Added display of follower count for search results
- Improved sorting of search results (by rank and then by number of followers)
- Added useful search tips
- Improved UI for search results with more feedback

## Added note on user search:
NIP-50 search sometimes fails to find certain usernames. However, users can always be found reliably by searching directly for their npub.

## UI improvements:
- Clear error and success messages
- Improvements in responsive design
- Improved accessibility through correct ARIA names

Corrections #9

body:
This pull request delivers a fully functional dark theme for the entire application, providing users with an alternative visual experience that reduces eye strain in low-light environments and caters to personal preferences. It's a big deal, a really professional touch.

Here's a detailed breakdown of the changes:

- **`theme.tsx` - Theme Definition:**
    - Introduced a distinct `DarkTheme` object, mirroring the structure of `LightTheme` but with a carefully selected dark color palette. This includes specific colors for background (`#282828`), text (`#FFFFFF`), primary buttons (`#BB86FC`), secondary elements, and more. We're talking about a complete visual overhaul option here.
    - Ensured that all theme properties defined in the `ThemeType` interface are implemented in both `LightTheme` and `DarkTheme` for consistency across the application. No half-measures here, folks.

- **`ThemeContext.tsx` - Theme Switching Logic:**
    - Modified the `ThemeProvider` component to manage the application's theme state using `useState`. It now holds a boolean `isDarkMode` to track the active theme.
    - Implemented the `toggleTheme` function, which flips the `isDarkMode` state, triggering a re-render and applying the corresponding theme. Simple and effective, the way things should be.
    - The `theme` value provided by the context dynamically selects either `LightTheme` or `DarkTheme` based on the `isDarkMode` state. This is the core mechanism for theme switching.
    - The `useTheme` hook is provided for easy access to the current theme, the `toggleTheme` function, and the `isDarkMode` status from any component within the `ThemeProvider`. Very user-friendly.

- **`App.tsx` - Theme Provider Integration:**
    - The root `AppNavigator` component is now wrapped with the `ThemeProvider`. This makes the theme context and the ability to switch themes available to all screens and components in the application. It's integrated right at the top, the best place.

body: Running ```pkg-config -libs``` with the .pc file produced by the vcpkg opencv4 with the freetype feature enabled includes this problematic output: -lharfbuzz::harfbuzz which causes the linker to never find it because it's actually called libharfbuzz.a. body:
This pull request introduces several new features and updates to enhance authentication, authorization, and file storage functionality. Key changes include the addition of OTP-based login, password reset flows, role-based permissions, and updates to the database models to support these features. Below is a categorized summary of the most important changes:

### Authentication Enhancements
* Added OTP-based login flow, including `OTPSession` model and `verify_otp` endpoint, to improve user authentication security (`app/db/models.py`, `app/route/v1/controllers/auth.py`, `app/route/v1/providers/auth.py`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-aefa0eb060f50e3b4f36098d47a41aaffbf27dc620711282ca404b95f88d70a3L49-R134) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c1fea61bc48d5ed30903b665d7551f6f235a883cb619422a24f2a834321d2ea6L39-R114) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-22d78e55920ca0b38eb049d0587fdff9ced6d333a17782a22ea4048178d87d95L106-R279)
* Implemented password reset functionality with `PasswordResetTicket` model and related endpoints (`password_reset_request` and `password_reset`) to allow users to securely reset their passwords (`app/db/models.py`, `app/route/v1/controllers/auth.py`, `app/route/v1/providers/auth.py`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-aefa0eb060f50e3b4f36098d47a41aaffbf27dc620711282ca404b95f88d70a3L49-R134) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c1fea61bc48d5ed30903b665d7551f6f235a883cb619422a24f2a834321d2ea6L39-R114) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-22d78e55920ca0b38eb049d0587fdff9ced6d333a17782a22ea4048178d87d95L106-R279)

### Role-Based Permissions
* Introduced `Role` and `Permission` models to support role-based access control, along with utility methods for creating and checking permissions (`app/db/models.py`, `app/security/permissions.py`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-aefa0eb060f50e3b4f36098d47a41aaffbf27dc620711282ca404b95f88d70a3L28-R78) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e148649e77632f8ff5d1c91930b5fd36d3dc7fb333ef4170a7764f9e08336759R1-R228)
* Added `PermissionChecker` class to streamline permission validation for resources and actions (`app/security/permissions.py`).

### Database Model Updates
* Extended `User` model with relationships for roles, OTP sessions, login sessions, and password reset tickets to support the new authentication and authorization features (`app/db/models.py`).
* Replaced `Media` model with `FileResource` to align with updated file storage functionality (`app/db/models.py`, `app/services/storage.py`). author: uz9
body:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9106e18a-496c-4310-85d4-601b9d9ea442



# Overview

This PR is a major rework of the pseudocode sidebar internals and a complete overhaul of the pseudocode animations. Most notably, the old canvas animations have been entirely moved to the sidebar as shown in the animation above.

# Problem

With the addition of the pseudocode sidebar, there is now duplicate code present between the sidebar and the canvas animation. Although this is mostly fine, there were a few issues I found when using it:

- We have two pseudocode buttons: one for switching between English/Code/None in the top right, and the one under the Pseudocode section that only toggles between English and Code. The buttons are somewhat synchronized, but the None option was only for not showing the canvas animation code--leading to some overall confusion. You can set the top right button to None, and the pseudocode sidebar tab will appear completely blank.

- The pseudocode text is a little outdated compared to the recent UI overhaul. The text is a different font, has no syntax highlighting, and is smaller and harder to read than the current sidebar aesthetic. 

- The old pseudocode animations would be a major headache for any attempts to create a proper mobile view for the site. They can't be easily adjusted like any other web component, and have fixed X/Y positions defined for every algorithm. The duplicate buttons and data also contribute to this, as now you have twice the amount of information to somehow fit on the screen.

# Changes

(It looks like a massive amount of files were changed due to each algorithm requiring slight animation tweaks, but the vast majority of this is just search/replace)

- Removed a fair bit of extra re-renders in the pseudocode sidebar component 

- Separated `AlgoScreen` into individual components for readability 

- Removed all Canvas highlighting and replaced it with the sidebar panel 

- Removed the old English/Code/none button in the top right. As the sidebar now has an explciit pseudocode tab, there doesn't seem to be a need for hiding it anymore, and having both that button and the toggle button on the sidebar was quite confusion (e.g. you could have an empty pseudocode page)

- Moved the pseudocode to be one scrollable block instead of individual sections. This is mostly for animation purposes, as some methods (e.g. addFront for ArrayList) internally call another method. Space is a bit cramped, but with dynamic scaling this will likely be less of an issue. 

- Moved the pseudocode language toggle button to the top right of the code block

- Removed all code elements from individual algorithms, as they're now managed automatically

- Moved all pseudocode-related procedures to the dedicated `Pseudocode` component 

- Abstracted most of the modal sidebar, there's more to be done here but this PR was already getting quite long 

- Standardized the `pseudocode.json` names to match the site URLs: there was a discrepancy between the two (e.g. Prims vs Prim) requiring additional processing. After this PR, all psuedocode json names should match the **page URLs**. The JSON had arguably better names, but I didn't want to risk breaking any Canvas links. 

- Moved LCS pseudocode back to the JSON file. It seems like this was already commented out and not doing anything, but the pseudocode at the very least still shows up in both languages. I assume this might be finished up in a later PR. 

- Migrated all algorithms to new pseudocode animation.


# For future work on algorithm animations 

The process for each individual algorithm stays almost exactly the same. The only few differences:

- There is no longer a need for hardcoded CODE_X and CODE_Y positions, and addCodeToCanvasBaseAll is no longer required whatsoever. These are now completely automatic.
- All highlights now take in the method name instead of code ID. Example:

```js 
this.highlight(0, 0, this.addFBCodeID);
```

becomes

```js 
this.highlight(0, 0, "addFB"); // these are the method names found in pseudocode.json
```

# Testing 

With this requiring slight modification of each algorithm, there's a nonzero chance I accidentally set the wrong animation for one of the methods. I'll be looking through each algorithm method by method, but if anyone is willing to double check these it would be fantastic. Thanks! 

# Changes remaining 

- [x] Remove the rest of the old highlighting code 
- [x] Switch setHighlight to its own dedicated method instead of hijacking AnimationMain's `setHighlight`--this will become `setCodeHighlight`
- [ ] Look through every algorithm animation and ensure it works
- [x] Verify undo history still works

author: 8beeeaaat
body:
This pull request introduces significant updates to the project, including transitioning to Docker-based workflows, upgrading Node.js versions, and enhancing documentation and configuration files. The changes aim to improve the development experience, simplify deployment, and provide better support for integration with TouchDesigner and AI agents.

### Docker and Deployment Enhancements:
* Added a `Dockerfile` to build the project with Node.js 24 and included Java runtime for OpenAPI Generator. The Docker image is configured to build and run the application. (`Dockerfile`)
* Introduced a `docker-compose.yml` file to manage the MCP server container, with configurations for ports, environment variables, and Docker networking. (`docker-compose.yml`)
* Updated the `Makefile` to include a `build` target for creating and extracting Docker-built modules. (`Makefile`)

### Node.js and Dependency Updates:
* Upgraded Node.js from version 22.x to 24.x across all workflows (`development.yml`, `release.yml`) and runtime configurations. (`.github/workflows/development.yml`, `.github/workflows/release.yml`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-73aefd4c5a252c08017de5edafa094a95ee6031e37832d96a4ff247563a57833L18-R18) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-87db21a973eed4fef5f32b267aa60fcee5cbdf03c67fafdc2a9b553bb0b15f34L19-R19) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-87db21a973eed4fef5f32b267aa60fcee5cbdf03c67fafdc2a9b553bb0b15f34L61-R61)
* Updated dependencies in `package.json`, including `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` to version 1.11.1 and `zod` to version 3.24.4. Dev dependencies like `@types/node` and `msw` were also updated. (`package.json`)

### Configuration and Environment Updates:
* Added a `dotenv` file template with detailed comments to support both Docker and Node.js environments. (`dotenv`)
* Modified `orval.config.ts` to dynamically set the base URL for API generation based on environment variables. (`orval.config.ts`)
* Introduced an `openapitools.json` configuration file for OpenAPI Generator CLI. (`openapitools.json`)

author: wireddown
body:
## Summary

This change adds a GUI application named `data-viewer` that opens a CSV data log file for plotting, exploration, replaying, and exporting.

Start it with **`qtpy-datalogger run data-viewer`**

Closes #73 

## Design

**apps/data_viewer.py** -- ✨ new file
This app opens CSV data log files and plots them

On launch, the user can open a CSV file, or they can demo the app with a generated data set. Once the data set loads, the app plots each measurement data series in a matplotlib figure.

Behaviors
- toggle the visibility of plots from the View menu
- pan and zoom the graph from the lower-right toolbar
- reload the data set from file
- replay the acquisition
- export the enabled plots for the rendered time span

Expected file format

| timestamp | measurement 1 | ... | measurement N |
|---|---|---|---|
| number or datetime | sample 1 | ... | sample 1 |
| larger value | sample 2 | ... | sample 2 |
| ... | ... | ... | ... |
| highest value | sample M | ... | sample M |

Export a demo data set to see an example.

**datatypes.py**
- Add new value named `Source` to `Links` that uses the URL for the project's source code

**guikit.py**
- Use capitalized theme names for the theme combobox
- Add function `hex_string_for_style()` -- Return the '#RRGGBB' string for the specified style name for the active or specified theme

**ttkbootstrap_matplotlib.py**
- Subscribe the wrapped matplotlib elements to the Tk event named `<Expose>`
  - Supports themes when the GUI's behavior covers and reveals subsections
- Automatically grid the Tk canvas used by matplotlib
  - Client convenience
- Add new function `apply_legend_style()` -- Apply the specified theme to the matplotlib Legend


**matplotlib_demo.py**
- Apply API updates

**pyproject.toml**

New dependencies
- pandas
  - Load and export the CSV files as DataFrames
- tkfontawesome
  - Adds [FontAwesome](https://github.com/FortAwesome/Font-Awesome) glyphs as SVG paths

## Screenshots or logs

author: buddhika75
body:
Closes #12266 - enable in app download of payara log files

The log‑download feature is now fully integrated. After deploying this branch, administrators can retrieve any Payara log file directly from the application by opening **Administration → Manage Metadata → System Administrator Function**. Click Download Log Files button to go to the Download Log Files Page.

The page presents the familiar “From / To” calendars, lists the matching `server.log` files, and streams the chosen file in one click.

Please remember to set the configuration option **“Location of the Payara Log”** to the absolute path of your instance’s `…/domains/domain1/logs` directory before using the page. If the path is missing or incorrect the table will remain empty, so this single setting must be saved per environment.

All code is view‑scoped, uses existing PrimeFaces components only, and includes the attribution comment requested for ChatGPT contributions. No further database changes are required.

With that the issue is resolved and ready for merge.

author: adrianlyjak
body:
# Description

This is currently a very rough exploration in implementing a temporal backend for llama index workflows.

The idea would be that you could install this integration, and run your workflow in a temporal runtime, instead of the local runtime. This could eventually support temporal features like: distributed runtime, temporal based retries, and workflow durability.

See `test.py` at https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/pull/18692/files#diff-10b69c7930230b44f8cf730bdfa7ce09e3c92139a6d6cb8e5d42f63c0b2621e0 for example of what this would look like.

I'm not sure this is a good idea, but it was intriguing enough for me to get this very rough proof of concept running. I so far only got it running so far as to be able to run the workflow in the `test.py` successfully.

author: ansuel
body:
With some extra inspection of checks.c of the dtc tool, it was finally discovered how DTC actually parse the PCI reg address.

In details it defined as bridge@device,function

- device is in the mask 0xf800 that is GENMASK(15, 11)
- function is in the mask 0x700 that is GENMASK(10, 8)

Hence to translate a bridge@1,0 0x00000800 should be used that sets
- device to 0x1 (0x800)
- function to 0x0 (0x0)

With this change these following warning gets muted.

arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/ipq8072-wpq873.dts:473.13-478.4: Warning (pci_device_reg): /soc@0/pci@10000000/bridge@1,0: PCI unit address format error, expected "0,0"
arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/ipq8072-haze.dts:303.13-318.4: Warning (pci_device_reg): /soc@0/pci@10000000/bridge@1,0: PCI unit address format error, expected "0,0"
arch/arm64/boot/dts/qcom/ipq8072-ax9000.dts:566.13-582.4: Warning (pci_device_reg): /soc@0/pci@10000000/bridge@1,0: PCI unit address format error, expected "0,0"

Update any affected DTS to the correct reg value.

---

@robimarko magic magic :D it was easier then expected.
(This is a continuation of #18106)

ChatGPT also say that GENMASK(23, 16) is PCI bus number.

So is it correct that bridge@1,0 refers to device,function ? 

Or should be PCI bus,device ???

Also any idea for the wifi node? Should that match the bridge value?

author: polarathene
body:
## Describe your changes

This PR does some minor revisions to `Dockerfile.md` docs + the `docker-3.2.yml` workflow as detailed in their commits.

- The docs are now using [GH Alerts](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/writing-on-github/getting-started-with-writing-and-formatting-on-github/basic-writing-and-formatting-syntax#alerts) syntax for displaying notes.
- In addition to the `Dockerfile-alpine` to `Dockerfile.alpine` rename, it also corrects the CI workflow ([which is presently failing](https://github.com/testssl/testssl.sh/actions/workflows/docker-3.2.yml)) to use the updated `GIT_BRANCH` build arg instead of the previous `BUILD_VERSION` build arg (_introduced recently via_ https://github.com/testssl/testssl.sh/pull/2752).

---

**NOTE:**
- We could also consider removing the need for the build arg in CI by preferring the `dist-local` stage. This would be implicit if we swap the `dist-git` + `dist-local` stage order of appearance in the `Dockerfile` to match the openSUSE `Dockerfile` since the last stage is the default one to build.
- [`dist-git` is effectively redundant](https://github.com/testssl/testssl.sh/pull/2758#issuecomment-2853244152) and could be dropped in favor of the alternative shown in the `Dockerfile.md` docs (_which makes no mention of these two final stages, as there isn't a need to raise awareness_).

  That said the UX may not be as pleasant, so you could keep the `dist-git` stage for a niche use-case if you think it's worthwhile? 🤷‍♂️ 

  Proposed (without `dist-git`):

  ```bash
  docker build --tag localhost/testssl.sh:3.2 https://github.com/testssl/testssl.sh.git#3.2

  # Alpine variant requires `--file`:
  docker build \
    --tag localhost/testssl.sh:3.2-alpine \
    --file https://raw.githubusercontent.com/testssl/testssl.sh/3.2/Dockerfile-alpine \
    https://github.com/testssl/testssl.sh.git#3.2
  ```

  Proposed (_if keeping `dist-git`, but as an opt-in target instead_) with a local `Dockerfile` copy, but remote source:
  
  ```bash
  # NOTE: Only cloning for the `Dockerfile`
  git clone --branch 3.2 --depth 1 https://github.com/testssl/testssl.sh .
  
  # Optional - Set the `GIT_URL` build arg too if preferring a fork instead of upstream repo:
  docker build \
    --tag localhost/testssl.sh:3.2-alpine \
    --target dist-git \
    --build-arg GIT_BRANCH=3.2 \
    .
  ```

  The main benefit of the latter with a `dist-git` target is that the user doesn't have to think about the two different URL inputs (_shouldn't be much of a concern, they'd likely copy/paste from docs and it's either a one off or automated script, assuming you actually have any users that care about this support in the first place_).

  Either way, you could have automated CI builds at a single branch that changes `GIT_BRANCH` to official releases or some PR branch/fork, that's the main benefit, but as documented this would work fine with `dist-local` with a remote context URL to a repo + branch.

  If they really care about size they should prefer `dist-local` with manual `git clone` so that `.dockerignore` can be used to shave off another 8MB.

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Improvement
- [x] Documentation update
